title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp.45-47): S is a regular connected Q-scheme with a geometric point xi: Spec C -> S, and Mot(S) is the category of smooth motives over S. Grothendieck lists 'fibre functors with extra structure' on Mot(S) that should be fully faithful, each conditional on a standard conjecture. Page 45 gave the Hodge/de Rham versions at the generic point. This page gives two more.

(2) 'Via Tate'. Let pi = pi_1(S, xi) be the étale fundamental group and l a prime. To M associate the pair {T_B(M_xi), rho_M^l}. Here T_B(M_xi) is the rational Betti realization of the fibre. rho_M^l : pi -> Aut_{Q_l}(T_B(M_xi) (x) Q_l) uses the comparison of Betti (x) Q_l with étale cohomology. In other words, this is a lisse Q_l-sheaf on S with a Q-structure on one fibre (marginal note: 'l-Modules galoisiens - faisceaux').
- A first attempt is crossed out: it used T_{B-H}, the Betti realization with its Hodge bigrading.
- Claim: if S is essentially of finite type over Q, the functor is fully faithful, assuming 'in part' the Tate conjecture and using 'results of Griffiths'.
- Check: let V = Hom_Q(T_B M_xi, T_B N_xi) and W = Hom_Mot(S)(M,N) inside V. Tate over the function field of S, together with surjectivity pi_1(eta) -> pi_1(S) for S regular, gives W (x) Q_l = (V (x) Q_l)^pi. Then V ∩ (V (x) Q_l)^pi = W, so the rational version follows.
- The phrases 'en partie' and 'Griffiths' suggest a reduction: assume Tate only in some range (e.g. over number fields), then pass to higher transcendence degree via Hodge-theoretic results on variations, i.e. what became the theorem of the fixed part.

Complex variant. If S is locally of finite type over C, replace pi by the topological pi' = pi_1(S(C), xi), with rho_M : pi' -> Aut_Q(T_B(M_xi)). One must then replace T_B by T_{B-H}, i.e. the local system plus the Hodge structure at the single point xi. The margin says 'here it is the Hodge conjecture one uses'. Modern justification: Hom of local systems is the space of pi'-invariants in the fibre Hom. By the theorem of the fixed part this is a sub-Hodge structure. Its Hodge classes are global flat Hodge classes, which the Hodge conjecture (variational form) makes algebraic.

Non-finite-type affine S: replace pi by a projective system of fundamental groups of finite-type models over Q.

(3) To M associate (T_DR(M), sigma, T_B(M_xi), phi):
- T_DR(M) is the relative algebraic de Rham cohomology, a filtered coherent O_S-module;
- sigma is its Gauss-Manin stratification relative to a fixed algebraically closed base field k (e.g. Q-bar);
- phi : T_DR(M)(xi) ≅ T_B(M_xi) (x) C is the comparison isomorphism.
The added note says it suffices to give the Hodge filtration on the single fibre T_DR(M)(xi). This is rigidity: horizontal morphisms are determined at one point, and global flat sections carry a Hodge structure by the fixed-part theorem. Claim: for S of finite type over k the functor is fully faithful, granting the Hodge conjecture and using Griffiths.

This prepares item (4) on p.47. There the filtration is dropped and Grothendieck asks whether the bare de Rham-Betti realization {T_DR, T_B, phi} over Q-bar is fully faithful, reformulated via a point g in G(C)/G(Q-bar) of the motivic Galois group. That is the Grothendieck period conjecture circle.
errors: No real error. The Q-structure version in (2) is correctly deducible from the Q_l-statement of Tate, since V ∩ (W (x) Q_l) = W.

'Griffiths' is invoked without precise statement. In 1965 the theorem of the fixed part and semisimplicity of geometric monodromy were not yet proved; they came with Griffiths 1968-70 and Deligne 1971. The full faithfulness claims in the complex variant and in (3) need exactly these results, so 'using Griffiths' is an anticipation rather than an available theorem.

In (3) it is implicit that S must be connected and that morphisms of filtered flat bundles compatible with phi at xi descend to motives. This needs the variational Hodge conjecture (algebraicity of flat classes that are Hodge at one point), which is stronger in appearance than the pointwise Hodge conjecture. Grothendieck lumps it under 'conj. de Hodge'.
The final marginal remark (k = Q not algebraically closed; where to put the filtration) is garbled and its precise content is unclear.

ideas.what: Fully faithful l-adic realization of motives over a base S of finite type over Q: lisse Q_l-sheaf with Q-structure at a geometric fibre, conditional on Tate.
ideas.modern_name: Tate conjecture over finitely generated fields / relative (family) Tate conjecture; full faithfulness of the l-adic realization of motivic sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tate (1963-64) for the conjecture; Grothendieck/Deligne folklore for the relative form
ideas.where_published: Tate conjecture discussed in Grothendieck's 'Standard conjectures' (1969) context; relative form not explicitly

ideas.what: Over C: the motive over S is determined by the topological local system plus the Hodge structure at one point (Hom = pi_1-invariant Hodge classes), via Hodge conjecture + Griffiths.
ideas.modern_name: Theorem of the fixed part + variational Hodge conjecture; rigidity of VHS of geometric origin
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1970), Deligne (Hodge II, 1971) for the fixed part; Grothendieck (1966 de Rham paper footnote) for the variational Hodge conjecture
ideas.where_published: On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, Publ. IHES 29 (1966), footnote on variational Hodge conjecture

ideas.what: Realization by filtered de Rham module with Gauss-Manin stratification relative to an algebraically closed k, Betti fibre, comparison; filtration needed only at one point.
ideas.modern_name: Relative de Rham-Betti / Hodge realization of motives over a base; filtered flat bundle (VHS) realization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz-Oda (Gauss-Manin, 1968), Deligne; de Rham-Betti structures: André, Bost-Charles
ideas.where_published: Gauss-Manin/stratification ideas in Grothendieck's crystals (Dix exposés, 1968); not this statement

ideas.what: Reduction of the non-finite-type case to a projective system of fundamental groups of finite-type models over Q.

missed.claim: Grothendieck suggests the Tate-type full faithfulness over S of finite type over Q needs Tate only 'in part', supplemented by Griffiths-type Hodge results. This hints at a reduction of the Tate conjecture over finitely generated fields of characteristic 0 to a smaller case (presumably number fields) using variation-of-Hodge-structure arguments. Such reductions appear in the modern literature (specialization arguments of André, Ambrosi, Morrow, mostly for divisors), apparently without reference to this 1965 idea.
missed.quote: est ess. de type fini sur Q, en admettant en partie la conj. de Tate, et utilisant rés. de Griffiths
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the 'reduce Tate over f.g. fields to number fields via fixed-part/specialization' strategy. The text is too terse to reconstruct a precise argument.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, early (1965) list of conditional full-faithfulness statements for realizations of motives over a base: l-adic, local system + one Hodge structure, and filtered Gauss-Manin + Betti. It anticipates the fixed-part theorem and the variational Hodge conjecture, the latter published by Grothendieck in 1966. Mostly folklore today; the cryptic 'Tate en partie + Griffiths' remark is the only mildly unusual hint.
transcription_corrections: 'Sous π = π1(S,ξ)' should read 'Soit π = π1(S,ξ)'.
The margin '(Via Tate)' is a correction over an earlier '(Via Hodge?)' parallel to p.45; the boxed marginal note reads 'ℓ-Modules galoisiens - faisceaux'.
The left margin note likely reads 'ici c'est la conj. [de] Hodge qu'on utilise !' rather than 'ici chaque conj. Hodge pour utiliser !'.
In (3), 'moyennant conj. de Hodge' appears with a correction, possibly 'conj. de Hodge(s)'; also 'conj. de Tate' replaces a struck-out 'Hodge' in (2).

The final left margin note is largely illegible. It seems to say that if S is of finite type (and k = Q̄ or not algebraically closed) one should put the filtration only on T_DR(M)(ξ) (the fibre at ξ); the reading 'demeure' and 'de plus bas' is doubtful.
Struck text in (2) reads roughly: 'où T_{B-H}(M_ξ) est la structure de Hodge associée à M_ξ, T_{B-H}(M) = {T_B(M_ξ) + bigraduation de T_B(M_ξ)⊗_Q C}'.
